label: a6-098-thm-closure-characterised-by-nets
tail:
### No fatal defects found

I have scrutinised every step of the proof and cross-checked each citation against the verbatim dependency text provided.  

**Forward direction (closure ⇒ net).**  
The construction of the index set  
\( E = \{(N,a) : N \in \mathcal{N}(p),\; a \in N \cap A\} \)  
is a valid set in ZF. The order defined by \( (N,a) \preceq (M,b) \iff M \subseteq N \) makes \(E\) a preordered set. Step 2.1 shows it is directed: for any two elements \( (N,a),(M,b) \) the set \( N\cap M \) is a neighbourhood (by [L2]) and meets \(A\) (by [L1]); picking any \(c \in (N\cap M)\cap A\) gives \( (N\cap M,c) \in E \) which is above both. No choice is used – only the non‑emptiness of the intersection, which follows from [L1] and \(p\in\overline{A}\).  

Step 2.2 verifies convergence: for a given neighbourhood \(N\) of \(p\), the non‑emptiness of \(N\cap A\) yields an \(a\) with \((N,a)\in E\); for every \((M,b) \succeq (N,a)\) one has \(M \subseteq N\), hence \(b \in M \subseteq N\), so the net is eventually in \(N\). By [L3] it converges to \(p\). Again no uniform choice is needed; the reasoning is a simple ∀∃ proof.

**Reverse direction (net ⇒ closure).**  
If a net in \(A\) converges to \(p\), then by [L3] it is eventually in every neighbourhood of \(p\); in particular each neighbourhood contains an element of the net, which lies in \(A\). Hence every neighbourhood meets \(A\), and [L1] gives \(p\in\overline{A}\).

**Citations.**  
- [L1] exactly matches the equivalence (a)⇔(b) in `thm-closure-characterisation-top`.  
- [L2] exactly matches consequence 3 of `def-neighbourhood-top`.  
- [L3] exactly matches the definition of convergence in `def-net-convergence-and-cluster-point`.

**Choice.** The proof uses no choice principle beyond ZF, so no missing hypothesis of that class is present.  

**Title.** The title matches the statement proved.

I found no mathematical inaccuracies, no unlicensed inferences, and no citation of a dependency for a claim it does not make.

0 fatal, 0 nonfatal
